title: Safehouse and Extraction
premise: Hazel Delacroix runs unattributed protection for clients who can't afford paper trails, so when a man named Elias Voss repays a favor she has no memory of doing, she knows the debt is manufactured — and that someone wants her inside his operation. Voss needs her to extract Dr. Ilse Brandt, a financial analyst defecting from a Frankfurt syndicate with evidence of market manipulation timed to detonate at Monday's opening bell. As Hazel moves Brandt across Europe through safehouses that keep getting burned, she realizes Brandt may be bait designed to flush out Hazel's own network, and that Voss's 'favor' was staged using a memory she lost after a job gone wrong in Riga. In the end, Hazel turns the trap around: she delivers a decoy to the syndicate's buyers while smuggling the real evidence out through the one channel they never watch, choosing justice outside the law over the clean exit Voss offers — and finally recovering what happened in Riga.
about_author: Ansel Brightwater is the pen name of a former logistics coordinator for executive protection firms who spent a decade moving people quietly across borders before turning to fiction. He writes from a coastal town whose location he declines to confirm.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A quiet week between contracts ends when Elias Voss appears at her office claiming she saved his life in Riga two years ago — a city she cannot remember visiting. He offers payment for a job: extract a defector before Monday. Emotional beat: unease masked as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: Ledger of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Hazel audits her own records and finds a two-week gap in Riga, expensed but undocumented. Her fixer, Marek, goes silent when she asks. POV alternates with Voss meeting his handler, revealing the debt story was scripted for him too. Beat: dread taking root.

chapters.title: The Client Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: Voss introduces the principal: Dr. Ilse Brandt, holed up in a Vienna safehouse with encrypted drives tied to a Frankfurt syndicate. Hazel insists on vetting Brandt herself and finds her terrified but precise. Beat: reluctant respect between two guarded women.

chapters.title: Terms of Extraction
chapters.summary: Hazel drafts the route — Vienna to Trieste by road, ferry north — while Voss pushes an air option she distrusts. First sign of surveillance: a parked car with diplomatic plates. Beat: the plan hardens even as trust frays.

chapters.title: Riga, Unremembered
chapters.summary: Flashback fragments surface: cold water, a name called underwater, hands pulling her out. Hazel digs into medical records and finds a concussion report she never filed. Beat: grief for a self she can't access.

chapters.title: First Move
chapters.summary: Extraction begins. Hazel moves Brandt out of Vienna during a power cut she suspects was engineered as cover — by whom, unclear. A tail is made and dropped in the Prater. Beat: adrenaline sharpening into focus.

chapters.title: Burned House
chapters.summary: The first safehouse near Graz is already compromised when they arrive; a dead courier sits at the kitchen table. Hazel realizes only four people knew the location. Beat: paranoia becomes method.

chapters.title: Marek's Silence
chapters.summary: Marek resurfaces, half-willing, and lets slip that Hazel's old crew ran a Riga op for the same syndicate. He refuses to say more and warns her off Voss. Beat: loyalty curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Trieste Crossing
chapters.summary: Night ferry north. Brandt opens up about the manipulation scheme — synthetic positions built on stolen settlement data. Hazel notices Voss photographing manifests. Beat: intimacy aboard the ship, undercut by doubt.

chapters.title: What Voss Owes
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. His handler squeezes him: deliver Brandt or his sister pays. He believes the Riga debt is real because the file is convincing. Beat: a decent man complicit in something rotten.

chapters.title: The Bait Hypothesis
chapters.summary: Hazel maps every leak back to the extraction itself and voices it aloud: Brandt isn't the prize, she's the lure — the drives are decoys meant to expose Hazel's network. Brandt neither confirms nor denies. Beat: cold clarity.

chapters.title: Split Routes
chapters.summary: Hazel splits the team: a visible convoy carrying decoy drives toward Munich, the real Brandt moving by rail with her alone. Voss insists on joining Hazel. Beat: commitment with no retreat.

chapters.title: Interrogation at the Border
chapters.summary: A routine check becomes a trap; Hazel talks them through with forged credentials while Voss nearly breaks cover. She realizes he's protecting someone, not himself. Beat: tension and a crack of empathy.

chapters.title: The Memory Returns
chapters.summary: In a mountain inn, the full Riga memory surfaces: Hazel pulled a drowning informant from the Danube canal — Voss's brother — and failed to save him. The 'favor' is real; the debt was weaponized. Beat: devastation and release.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Snow
chapters.summary: Hazel confronts Voss. He admits he didn't know the debt was scripted until mid-operation; his handler used his grief as leverage. They choose each other over their handlers. Beat: love against duty, declared plainly.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Countdown
chapters.summary: Saturday night. The syndicate moves early, hitting the decoy convoy and capturing the wrong drives. Hazel learns the buyers convene Sunday — one day ahead of schedule. Beat: the clock collapses.

chapters.title: The Decoy Delivered
chapters.summary: Hazel offers the syndicate a trade: Brandt for the network's immunity list. The handoff at a freight yard goes smoothly — too smoothly. She watches Brandt walk away and hates herself for it. Beat: sacrifice performed.

chapters.title: Double Blind
chapters.summary: Brandt, complicit all along, feeds the buyers corrupted data while Hazel's real package — the original settlement logs — moves through Marek's obscure channel: a church charity's document shipment. Beat: the trap inverted.

chapters.title: Monday, 9:00 CET
chapters.summary: Markets open; the manipulated positions unwind publicly as regulators receive the true logs simultaneously. The syndicate's buyers scatter. Voss's handler burns him, and he disappears into Hazel's channels. Beat: justice landing without permission.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: Hazel retrieves Brandt from a second safehouse — the trade was always planned as temporary custody, not betrayal. Brandt chooses testimony over disappearance. Beat: trust repaid.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Hazel visits Riga, stands at the canal, and lets the memory settle instead of running from it. She tells Voss the truth about his brother and what she couldn't do. Beat: mourning without absolution.

chapters.title: Safehouse and Extraction
chapters.summary: Weeks later, a new client arrives with an impossible request and no memory attached. Hazel takes the case on her terms, Voss beside her, the network rebuilt smaller and cleaner. Beat: continuation chosen knowingly — the life goes on, but owned this time.
